item.title: Political Networks: collaboration in the Constitutional Convention (2021–2022)
item.description: Chile’s Constitutional Convention (2021–2022) is a rare natural experiment for studying how political collaboration organizes from scratch: a majority of delegates with no prior political experience, a body that dissolved upon delivering its draft, and procedural rules written by its own members. Two of those rules structure the study. Each constitutional initiative required between 8 and 16 signatures, so signing amounted to forming a visible, dated coalition. In addition, each provision needed two thirds of the plenary (103 of 154 votes) to pass.

item.title: New publication in Applied Network Science: Same score, different network
item.description: PoliCICS researchers Jorge Fábrega and Aníbal Olivera published the article “Same score, different network: configuration-level heterogeneity in composite risk measures” in Applied Network Science. The work proposes a network-based framework for examining cases that share the same risk score but may differ in how their factors are organized. Using 17,272 administrative assessments from a criminological instrument applied by Chile’s prison service (Gendarmería de Chile), the authors show that identical scores can correspond to distinct, recurrent network architectures, and that some patterns of item co-presence are associated with recidivism.

item.title: Launch of Deputies Dataset 2002-2026
item.description: The PoliCICS laboratory is pleased to announce the launch of the Deputies Dataset 2002-2026, a new public resource developed by researcher Jorge Fábrega. This dataset provides systematic estimates of the ideological positions of all members of the Chilean Chamber of Deputies across six consecutive legislative periods. The estimates are based exclusively on roll-call votes related to bill proposals debated and voted on in plenary sessions, offering a robust tool for legislative analysis.
